newsitem.title: UK: ACPC not interested in sky-high prices -Barbosa.
newsitem.headline: ACPC not interested in sky-high prices -Barbosa.

text.p: Soaring coffee prices were of no concern yet to producers even thought they were leading to retail price hikes, Rubens Barbosa, president of the Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) said on Friday.

In a telephone interview with Reuters, Barbosa, the Brazilian ambassador to Britain, said the ACPC was not interested in sky-high prices, keeping its main objective as "stabilising prices at a remunerative level".
"As far as the ACPC is concerned we are not looking for sky-high prices," Barbosa said. "It is neither in the interest of the consumers nor the producers to have boom and bust cycles again," he said.
But there had been no requests from member states yet to hold an emergency meeting to assess the current market conditions after a 30-percent rise in futures prices since the beginning of this year.
"Our programme goes up until June, by then we will have had a meeting in May and we will be assessing the market," he said.

ACPC countries agreed additional cuts in exports of robusta and arabica coffee totalling 1.3 million bags in the first six months of 1997, aiming to narrow the premium of New York-traded arabica over London's robusta.
Barbosa denied comments that ACPC's export retention programme may have backfired, threatening consumer demand, saying the price spike was a result of changes in fundamental conditions.
"What we are seeing today is what we've been saying all along. There is a shortage of coffee but the market disconsidered that. There is still the negative effect in Brazil of the frost..."
He said consumer stocks had declined sharply and just-in-time policies adopted by roasters had introduced "a very dangerous element into the market".
